master_narrator.agency_handoff_prompt:
The Feast that night was different. It wasn't loud. It was warm.

The Stormbreaker hummed with captured energy. The Living Atlas glowed with a stable map. The Mycelial network pulsed with a gentle, rhythmic green. Sixteen mugs were raised in the warm circle of firelight while the captured geode hummed beneath the floorboards.

Elara scanned the room, her gaze sharp, tracking micro-cortisol baselines and radiation dosimetry for sixteen stubborn geniuses. Her focus rested on Silas. If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong, she thought, watching him fidget. She was determined to mitigate their Isolated-Confined-Extreme Third-Quarter cortisol cascades and autonomic hypervigilance through this structured communal roast ritual and some oxytocin vagal buffering.

She approached him, a steaming bowl of roasted vegetables covered in cheese in one hand. Silas, she said, her voice a warm but uncompromising command, sit down and eat your soup. And keep that grounded ankle wire attached. I don't care if you're eighty-two years old and invented the induction baffle; your blood pressure is high and your fingers are stiff.

He glared at her, but the warmth of the firelight and the undeniable logic of her clinical matriarch presence softened his resistance. He took the bowl. Under extreme stress, Elara could become the ruthless, unblinking triage commander, but tonight, she was the anchor.

As Silas took a bite, he offered a genuine, rare smile. To the rust, he murmured softly.

Elara nodded, feeling the room's tension collectively exhale. Healing was a shared practice, and tonight, in the quiet bioluminescent wonder of the cavern, they weren't just surviving. They were thriving.
